title: Training-Free Adversarial Robustness in Computational MRI

claims.text: The approach remains effective across attack strengths ε∈{0.01, 0.02}, outperforming adversarial training baselines at each strength (Section 4.4, Figure 4)

On three fastMRI datasets (Cor-PD knee, Cor-PDFS knee, Ax-FLAIR brain), the mitigation raises PSNR to 33.23-36.17 dB and SSIM to 0.92-0.94 (Cor-PD), 34.03-34.32 dB and 0.81-0.83 SSIM (Cor-PDFS), and 34.89-35.71 dB and 0.92-0.93 SSIM (Ax-FLAIR) (Table 1)

In a blind setting with unknown attack type/strength, a linear-scheduler estimation of ε and α achieves mitigation performance comparable to the informed (known-attack) setting (Section 4.4, Figure 6, Table 9)

The method detects adversarial attacks on MRI reconstruction by comparing normalized k-space errors ζ1 and ζ2 from cyclic re-undersampling, flagging an attack when ζ2−ζ1 exceeds a dataset-dependent threshold, without any model retraining (Section 3.2, Algorithm 1)
The method generalizes across five reconstruction architectures (MoDL, XPDNet, RIM, E2E-VarNet, Recurrent-VarNet), consistently reducing adversarial artifacts (Figure 5, Table 3)
Mitigation is performed via reverse projected gradient descent within an ε-ball that minimizes a cyclic measurement-consistency loss across multiple undersampling patterns (Section 3.3, Algorithm 2)
